read_scope.notes: Read the entire 22-page frozen PDF, including references and Appendices A–G, from page-delimited text and visually inspected every rendered page. Inspected Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–12 in the PDF. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve exact wording and locations. The technical appendices were treated as optional depth when judging main-text accessibility. Independently computed the supplied PDF SHA256. No other reviews, versions, progress records, or non-snapshot manuscript were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with useful distinctions stated in ordinary language before their formal versions. The median-lightness example and the three idealized generators in Section 4.1 make difficult concepts economical and concrete. Terms such as aligned response, error, scene variation and calibration remain consistent. The compressed sequence of abstract results and the definition-like opening of the Discussion leave small opportunities to improve emphasis and economy.
score_reasons.structure: The main text progresses coherently from the question through experimental arms, feature interpretation, contrast intuition, formal scores and five intelligibly ordered result subsections. Section 4.4 signals the retrospective status and purpose of the diagnostics before the results; detailed identities, controls and earlier cohorts are appropriately placed in appendices. The main narrative is self-sufficient. The Discussion could advance the evaluation implication more directly instead of briefly rehearsing the definitions immediately before the Conclusion.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: A new graduate-level reader can recover what was generated, what the finite digital reference target means, why the four-painter mean is removed, and why positive alignment need not imply low error. Table 1 translates feature families into recognizable image properties; Section 4.1 explains the zero/one error anchors; the Figure 1 control columns, Figure 2 detail panels and Figure 3 numerical heatmaps are interpretable. The theoretical no-distinction benchmark, repeat correction and unchanged images under calibration are explicitly distinguished. The abstract remains somewhat densely packed for a first encounter with these concepts.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening Monet/Sisley comparison poses a consequential and readily grasped evaluation problem. The common-scene image grid rewards comparison, and the results repeatedly explain what apparent contradictions reveal: near-unit alignment with substantial error, weak Monet–Sisley responses despite aggregate alignment, and ordering changes under averaging and rescaling. Headings sustain the narrative without hype. A more implication-led Discussion and a less compressed abstract would give these findings slightly stronger emphasis.

strengths: Section 4.1 connects an observed lightness difference (.325 versus .254 development-IQR units) to contrast centering, then uses no response, exact response and doubled response to explain the error benchmark before equations.

Figures 1–3 provide complementary evidence: directly inspectable prompt arms, reference-fitted geometry with magnified Monet/Sisley/Pissarro detail, and all-feature pair estimates with explicit scale anchors.

Section 5.4 makes the scene-versus-average distinction concrete with Nano Banana 2 and FLUX, and explains why shrinking GPT Image 2 can lower total mismatch even when its aligned amplitude starts near one.

The main text clearly labels retrospective calibration, pair diagnostics and corrected-source comparisons, including the changed Sunburst interval and the absence of improved or newly generated images.

Limitations remain tied to actual interpretation: the finite reproduction target, unvalidated perceptual meaning, fixed scenes, repeat assumptions and AI-only source audit are all disclosed without requiring the reader to inspect the repository.

findings.issue: The abstract stacks the shared fraction, uncertain absolute mismatch, pair failures, uncalibrated ordering and calibrated ordering in rapid succession. The separate sentence naming the uncalibrated minimum interrupts the explanatory connection to the following calibration sentence.
findings.reader_effect: A first-time reader must retain several unfamiliar comparison types while working out that the final model change results from rescaling measured contrasts. The facts are accurate, but their hierarchy is less immediate than in the main text.
findings.suggested_change: Combine the two ordering sentences into a single causal statement, for example: “Retrospective rescaling of measured contrasts, fitted on other scenes, changes the lowest-error estimate from FLUX.2 Max to GPT Image 2 without changing images.” Keep the single-factor detail in Sections 4.4 and 5.4, where it is already explicit. This shortens the abstract and preserves the evidence within the 155-word limit.

findings.issue: The Discussion begins by reintroducing what alignment, pair checks, scene error and calibration do, although these distinctions have just structured the Results. Its final sentence supplies the implication, but the paragraph spends most of its space repeating the explanatory map.
findings.reader_effect: The transition from results to interpretation briefly feels like another summary, especially because a separate Conclusion follows on the same page. The paper’s practical evaluation lesson receives less emphasis than its metric definitions.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the opening definition sequence with an implication grounded in the reported comparison, such as: “On this panel, the lowest total error alone does not identify the response that best preserves every painter distinction. Pair coverage, contrast magnitude and scene consistency explain why the model ordering changes.” Retain the subsequent causal limitation paragraph. This is a substitution, not added length.

summary: An excellent and largely self-contained account of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The intuitive methods, informative visual comparisons and explicit inferential boundaries make the scientific story readily recoverable. Remaining changes are localized improvements to abstract compression and discussion emphasis, not substantive reconstruction or requests for additional evidence.
